newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power firm, Dec sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power firm, Dec sharply higher.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. were firm, with Northwest prices particularly strong amid forecasts for cooler weather next week, market sources said Friday.
"Loads are up a bit. Temperatures are colder," said one Northwest trader.

Higher natural gas prices and statements by the Bonneville Power Administration that Pacific Intertie lines will remain curtailed at least through early next year were also cited as bullish market factors.

December California-Oregon border (COB) power was quoted at $25.00-25.40 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $24.10-24.35. Palo Verde for December was last quoted at $23.25-23.45, compared with $22.20-22.50.
Firm on-peak power for Monday at COB was last quoted at $23.00-24.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $22.50-23.00 for Friday.
Off-peak COB was quoted at $19.00-19.50, compared with $18.50-19.00.
Monday Mid-Columbia was quoted at $19.50-20.50, compared with $19.50-20.00 for Friday.
Firm on-peak Palo Verde was quoted at $20.00-21.00, compared with $20.00-20.50 per MWh for Friday deliveries. Four Corners was also quoted at $20.00-21.00, compared with $21.00-21.50.
